snapshot.retrieval_boundary: Selected N33, N34, N35, N54, and N76 cards/source-map excerpts; retrieval does not validate their claims or establish novelty.

overall_verdict: No defensible novelty or priority claim survived the current primary-literature and counterexample attacks. Retain the results below as scoped model bounds, measurement gates, and comparator audits.

claims.statement: For a capped protein count N in {0,...,M}, with only unit births of predictable intensity lambda_t <= B and independent per-molecule loss rate gamma, the process is pathwise dominated by the capped immigration-death chain with birth rate B and loss rate gamma. From common initial count, liminf_t P(N_t < h) >= [sum_{n=0}^{h-1} q^n/n!]/[sum_{n=0}^{M} q^n/n!], q=B/gamma.
assumptions: Single-molecule upward jumps only; no bursts or alternate protein-production routes.
Predictable causal birth intensity is uniformly bounded by B across all promoter, resource, and controller states.
The count has a hard ceiling M, with births blocked at M.
Each molecule has independent constant loss rate gamma>0; feedback does not reduce that rate.
The circuit process and comparator start at the same count.
claims.status: internally_reconstructed_model_result; bounded-rate immigration-death domination is established prior art; novelty not claimed
claims.novelty_boundary: Hemberg and Barahona (2007) already use a first-order immigration-death process to dominate bounded Hill/Monod gene-expression propensities and apply it to the toggle switch and repressilator. The finite-cap threshold-tail formula is a direct corollary. The result is a peak-cap screen, not a same-average-cost feedback comparison or a nature claim.

not_charged: growth-mediated dilution unless included in gamma

claims.falsifier: A process satisfying all stated assumptions but with liminf low-count probability below the truncated-Poisson tail would falsify the coupling claim. For a biological mapping, a birth-rate excursion above B, burst jump, state-dependent loss, or unmodeled production route invalidates the premise.
claims.next_gate: For one circuit, measure a uniform peak translation-completion cap, independent protein-loss rate, and copy ceiling; compare feedback with both a peak-matched saturated source and an average-cost-matched constitutive source.

claims.statement: In the exact finite chain M=10, gamma=1, state-dependent birth rate lambda_n=10-n has Binomial(10,1/2) stationary law, mean 5, dropout 1/1024, and P(N<5)=193/512. A constant attempted-birth source tuned to the same mean has rate approximately 5.1041217944, truncated-Poisson stationary law, dropout approximately 0.00616841, and P(N<5) approximately 0.42915. Thus feedback can improve these low-tail metrics at equal average accepted synthesis while using a larger peak rate.
assumptions: Birth-death chain on {0,...,10}.
Death rate is n in state n.
Feedback birth rate is 10-n and attempted births are blocked at 10.
The constant-rate baseline is calibrated to the same stationary mean; stationary mean accepted birth flux equals mean death flux.
claims.status: finite exact-law comparison with a numerically solved baseline parameter; illustrative model counterexample, not a novelty claim
claims.novelty_boundary: This only separates peak-resource and average-resource contracts. It is not a general optimality theorem for feedback, and a molecular implementation must charge controller molecules and the larger peak capacity.

same: mean accepted protein-production rate 5 per unit time

claims.falsifier: The exact binomial law, truncated-Poisson law, or their stated stationary-tail values fail under the specified transition rates.
claims.next_gate: Keep peak and average cost separate in any proposed reliability comparison; if implementing the policy, charge its sensing/feedback delay and molecular overhead.

claims.statement: For finite events X_i with marginals p_i, max(0, sum_i p_i-(m-1)) <= P(intersection_i X_i) <= min_i p_i, with both endpoints attainable. Per-guide marginal rates alone do not imply the product probability; independence or a measured joint repair model is required.
assumptions: X_i describe molecular escape of guide site i on one haplotype.
Only marginal probabilities are supplied for the bound.
The event model includes all structural escape routes relevant to cleavage; missed routes require an added error allowance.
claims.status: internally reconstructed standard Frechet coupling result; application is a principled rejection of marginal-only exponential suppression claims
claims.novelty_boundary: The inequality is standard; prior multiplex-drive studies already discuss deletions, resistance assumptions, and functional resistance. Recent experiments show multiplexing can also be useful. No claim that all multiplex drives fail.
claims.falsifier: A same-haplotype co-occurrence pattern inconsistent with the chosen independence model rejects that model. Functional resistance must be measured separately from molecular cut escape.
claims.next_gate: Measure per-guide marginals, joint all-site escape, and function on germline-origin transmissions; pre-register the desired risk ceiling and sequencing dropout bound.

claims.statement: For x in {0,1}^2 with latent phenotype f(x)=beta0+beta1*x1+beta2*x2+beta12*x1*x2 followed by an unrestricted unknown strictly increasing assay link g and independent Gaussian noise, there are an additive model beta12=0 and an epistatic model beta12=7 inducing identical observation distributions for every adaptive genotype-query strategy and every budget. The explicit observed means at genotypes 00,10,01,11 are 1,2,3,4 in both worlds, so total variation is zero and two-world minimax classification error is at least 1/2.
assumptions: Two biallelic loci and genotype set {0,1}^2.
The assay link is unknown and ranges over strictly increasing functions.
Measurement errors are independent N(0,sigma^2), including the zero-noise case.
A query selects one genotype and returns one assay measurement; selection may be randomized and adaptive.
claims.status: internally proved conditional observation-model theorem; scale-induced apparent epistasis is established prior art; no novelty claim
claims.novelty_boundary: Sailer and Harms (2017) already show nonlinear phenotype scales can induce apparent higher-order epistasis. This package makes an explicit all-adaptive-query observational-equivalence construction; exact priority for the formal packaging is unreviewed.

costs.unrestricted_link: No finite number of genotype queries resolves the latent-scale ambiguity.
costs.repair: External full-range calibration or a charged parametric/smoothness assumption is required.
costs.factorial_design: After calibration, four genotypes with r independent replicates require 4r phenotype measurements; calibration and batch costs are additional.

claims.falsifier: The theorem's premise is absent if the intended epistasis is defined directly on a verified calibrated assay scale or if an externally justified link restriction excludes the constructed pair.
claims.next_gate: Define the biological scale for epistasis before acquisition; calibrate independently and test the four-cell contrast on a held-out channel or run.

claims.statement: For independent receptor counts Y_i~Pois(mu_i) under H0 and Y_i~Pois(q*mu_i) under H1 with q=exp(delta/lambda), total expected count M=sum_i mu_i, and arbitrary downstream stochastic postprocessing, any binary decoder with worst-case error <= epsilon<1/2 requires M >= -log(4*epsilon*(1-epsilon))/(exp(delta/(2*lambda))-1)^2.
assumptions: Known exponential decay length and cell positions; the two hypotheses differ by a global profile shift delta.
Independent unsaturated Poisson counts are the full gradient information available to the program.
No unknown additive background, receptor heterogeneity, extra spatial cue, or event-count correlation.
Cell-cell communication and intracellular circuits are stochastic postprocessing of the count vector.
claims.status: proved model theorem; strong overlap with established positional-information and multicellular-sensing limits; novelty not claimed
claims.novelty_boundary: The exact finite-error test with total raw event count charged is a useful baseline, but the positional-noise, multicellular communication, boundary-refinement, and cost-precision literature substantially overlaps the problem. No organism-level claim follows without count-model validation.

costs.charged: Total expected receptor events M across all cells and all temporal samples in the observation window.

claims.falsifier: Non-Poisson or correlated biological observations invalidate the likelihood premise but do not falsify the conditional theorem. A biological application requires measured cell-resolved counts, dispersion, correlations, and profile parameters.
claims.next_gate: Match the exact bound to Tostevin et al. 2007 under the same geometry, observation time, receptor-event budget, and noise model; retain as baseline unless the comparison yields a distinct consequence.
